Investment to Accelerate iCareManager's Mission to be the System of Record for Intellectual and Developmental Disability and Human Services Providers
iCareManager receives growth investment from Five Elms Capital to build a leading AI-native platform for intellectual and developmental disability (IDD) care providers
Funding will modernize the platform, expand AI capabilities, extend go-to-market reach, and grow the senior leadership team
High-quality customer support remains core to the strategy as iCareManager serves a growing provider base
Five Elms brings deep experience scaling vertical AI-native software businesses
COLUMBIA, Md. , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- iCareManager, a leading EHR and care management platform purpose-built for providers supporting people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD), today announced a strategic growth investment from Five Elms Capital. The partnership will accelerate product innovation, expand AI capabilities, grow the leadership team, and extend iCareManager's reach to more provider organizations across the U.S.
Continue Reading
iCareManager
IDD providers operate in one of healthcare's most complex environments, navigating state-specific Medicaid waivers, service authorizations, billing, EVV, medication management, and compliance amid workforce shortages and financial pressure. Since 2011, iCareManager has simplified these challenges with technology built specifically for the IDD community.
iCareManager is a unified platform that connects clinical care, service delivery, compliance, workforce management, and billing for human services providers. It brings person-centered planning, eMAR, documentation, scheduling, and Medicaid billing into one view, with built-in support for state-specific rules and EVV. White-glove onboarding and ongoing support help providers adopt it with confidence.
"Over the years, we've built iCareManager with a clear purpose: to make technology work better for the people who provide support and care," said Kamal Sheikh, Co-Founder and CEO of iCareManager. "We're now entering a new era where AI will fundamentally change how people work and interact with technology. The next generation of software won't just help people manage their work; it will increasingly work alongside them. Five Elms understands what we've built, the market we serve, and where we want to go. This partnership gives us the resources and expertise to accelerate that vision, continue innovating, and bring more value to the providers who rely on us every day."
With Five Elms Capital's investment, iCareManager plans to advance the modernization of its technology platform while expanding its next generation of AI-enabled capabilities. "So much of a provider's day runs through iCareManager, from support plans and medication administration to compliance and billing, all on a single record," said Zach Gornet, Vice President at Five Elms Capital. "The AI capabilities the team is building will take real administrative weight off direct support professionals so they can spend more time with the people they serve."
Building on its integrated foundation, iCareManager is developing practical, responsible AI tools that simplify documentation, surface relevant information, and support clinical and operational decisions, reducing administrative work

articles.title: CIBC Innovation Banking: Growth Financing To Support PortX’s AI-Native Banking Integration Platform
articles.snippet:
CIBC Innovation Banking has provided growth capital financing to PortX, a Seattle-based financial technology company developing an AI-native integration platform for community banks and credit unions. The financing will support PortX's product development and expansion as financial institutions seek more efficient ways to connect banking systems, fintech applications, and payment networks.

articles.text:
CIBC Innovation Banking: Growth Financing To Support PortX’s AI-Native Banking Integration Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:46 AM
CIBC Innovation Banking: Growth Financing To Support PortX’s AI-Native Banking Integration Platform
CIBC Innovation Banking has provided growth capital financing to PortX, a Seattle-based financial technology company developing an AI-native integration platform for community banks and credit unions. The financing will support PortX’s product development and expansion as financial institutions seek more efficient ways to connect banking systems, fintech applications, and payment networks.
PortX provides application programming interface infrastructure designed to connect technologies that financial institutions use to manage accounts, process payments, and access customer information.
Its platform currently connects with more than 30 core banking systems and over 100 fintech applications.
It also supports payment connectivity involving the Automated Clearing House network, the Federal Reserve’s FedNow instant payment system, and wire transfers.
These integrations are intended to help community banks and credit unions modernize operations without replacing their existing core systems.
Smaller financial institutions frequently face challenges when adopting new technology because traditional banking platforms may require customized integrations with outside applications.
Developing and maintaining these connections can require substantial engineering resources, create additional operating expenses, and delay the introduction of new financial products.
PortX aims to address these issues through reusable infrastructure that connects multiple systems through a common integration framework.
The platform is designed to support real-time information exchange, application interoperability, and consistent data access.
PortX has also incorporated governance capabilities intended to support the adoption of AI within regulated financial institutions.
Its infrastructure allows activities to be logged, traced, and tracked, supporting oversight of automated processes and interactions across connected systems.
The company holds SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certifications, reflecting its investment in information security controls and management practices.
PortX believes these capabilities are increasingly important as banks and credit unions introduce AI tools into operations involving sensitive financial information.
The company reports that Sound Credit Union has reclaimed more than 10,000 business hours through its implementation of PortX technology.
This example highlights the potential for integrated banking infrastructure to reduce repetitive work and improve productivity.
PortX intends to use CIBC’s financing to support continued growth and develop additional platform capabilities.
The financing provides nondilutive capital, allowing the company to expand without issuing additional equity as part of the transaction.
PortX is backed by investors including Fuse, BankTech Ventures, Curql Collective, the American Bankers Association, EJF Capital, and Allied Solutions.
Its investor relationships represent participation from more than 350 financial institutions.
CIBC Innovation Banking provides financing to growth-stage technology and life sciences companies across North America.

articles.text:
Ring Launches With $249.99 Drone Cam And $999.99 Rover Cam For Autonomous Security
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:22 AM
Ring Launches With $249.99 Drone Cam And $999.99 Rover Cam For Autonomous Security
Ring, Amazon’s smart home security company, has announced Ring Robotics, a new category of autonomous security devices designed to patrol, investigate disturbances, and respond to potential threats across homes and businesses. The launch includes two products: Ring Drone Cam, a flying indoor security camera priced at $249.99, and Ring Rover Cam, a mobile security robot for businesses priced at $999.99.
The new product category expands Ring’s traditional security offerings, which have primarily relied on stationary cameras, video doorbells, motion sensors, and alarm systems.
Ring Robotics introduces mobile devices that can autonomously navigate indoor environments, investigate security alerts, and provide video coverage in areas that fixed cameras may not reach.
Both products are powered by AI Pilot, a proprietary navigation and intelligence system that combines cameras, computer vision models, on-device sensors, and cloud processing.
AI Pilot allows the devices to map indoor spaces, identify important locations, and navigate between designated patrol points.
During setup, users can carry Ring Drone Cam through their homes or allow Ring Rover Cam to explore a business environment autonomously.
The system analyzes the environment and generates a floor plan, automatically identifying rooms and suggesting locations that may require additional security attention.
These locations can include entrances, windows, cash registers, storage areas, and corridors.
Customers can customize patrol points and establish routes based on their security preferences.
Once a patrol begins, AI Pilot calculates a route to the selected destination while navigating around furniture, shelving, and other obstacles.
The technology is designed to reduce the manual effort associated with monitoring multiple areas of a property.
Ring Drone Cam For Residential Security
Ring Drone Cam is a flying indoor camera designed to provide security coverage throughout a home without requiring a stationary camera in every room.
The device remains docked when not in use and can be activated manually, through scheduled flights, or in response to compatible Ring security alerts.
Customers can establish custom flight routes and designate areas for the drone to inspect.
When a connected Ring camera, sensor, or alarm detects activity, Ring Drone Cam can automatically travel to previously configured patrol points.
The device provides 2K video resolution, a 148-degree field of view, and the ability to rotate 360 degrees.
Two integrated LED lights automatically activate in low-light conditions to improve visibility.
The camera integrates with existing Ring cameras, doorbells, sensors, and alarms.
Customers can also control the device through the new Alexa Home Map interface.
Ring envisions applications such as checking whether windows are closed before leaving home or investigating an unexpected security notification while traveling.
By allowing a single camera to move between rooms, Ring Drone Cam provides an alternative to installing multiple fixed indoor cameras.
The company plans to begin shipping Ring Drone Cam in the United States on January 27, 2027, at a retail price of $249.99.
